- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.25) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match true mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and model forecast is below recent 18-day average, model underestimates upward momentum; raise forecast by 2–5% to match sentiment-driven bias.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model exhibits lagged response; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 2–5% in early period (days 1–10) when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply +2% bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model fails to anticipate downward correction; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast from day 10 onward.
